entries.subject: USGS Dawn FC global mosaic at 140 m/pixel
entries.finding: Monochrome samples the orthorectified, body-fixed Dawn FC2 mosaic through WMS at 4096 by 2048 over 0-360 degrees east and 90N-90S; the PDS record documents a bundle-block adjustment using Dawn orbit and attitude, the high-resolution shape model and the Kait-anchored longitude system, so the image-to-Ceres frame is documented and no visual crater match is performed here. It is visible-light grayscale, not an unlit albedo map, and the release states the extreme south pole was unilluminated with gaps remaining.

entries.subject: Native DLR/USGS Dawn FC 140 m global mosaic cube (Ceres_Dawn_FC_DLR_global_59ppd_Feb2016.cub, the product behind NASA Trek's 59 ppd layer) instead of the WMS render
entries.finding: Not adopted. The Monochrome dataset already shows this mosaic, rendered by the USGS WMS at the full 4096 x 2048 prepared size, so the cube adds no resolution. Reduced by pixel-area mean to the same frame, it keeps the same tone (median transfer is identity) and registration (best shift 0, 0). Pixelmatch at threshold 0.1 flags 7.2% of the map, 7.8% after the WebP q80 lane on both and 1.4% at half resolution. Between 34 N and 11 S only 0.1-0.4% change; toward the poles 16-19% change, where the WMS render shows resampling jaggies the area mean does not. Switching needs a reader for tiled ISIS3 byte cubes that the shared reducer lacks, and the cube stores the south-polar gap as value 1, the same value as clipped shadow (11% of its pixels), so the gap cannot be told from terrain by value.
entries.revisitWhen: A shared reader for tiled ISIS3 byte cubes exists and DLR or USGS documents the cube's fill value, or the high-latitude crops are judged worth the change.

entries.subject: NASA PIA19977 false-colour map
entries.finding: Enhanced color uses the 3078 by 1537 false-colour image from 920, 750 and 440 nm filters, retained as a distinct map interpretation rather than calibrated monochrome; it keeps its published equirectangular map frame, and the review asserts no pixel-for-pixel pairing with the DTM.

entries.subject: Bright final columns of the PIA19977 source map
entries.finding: The last two columns of the enhanced-colour source are brighter than their neighbours, mean brightness 173 and 193 against about 135, so a thin light line can show along 0 degrees at close zoom.
entries.revisitWhen: A corrected release of the enhanced-colour map removes the bright edge columns.

entries.subject: DLR/USGS Dawn HAMO global DTM at 137 m
entries.finding: Elevation uses the 21,600 by 10,800 signed 16-bit DTM sampled without filling missing values, as metres above a 470 km sphere including the body's overall shape, mapped to a fixed -30 to +20 km scale with shading derived from neighbouring model heights.

entries.subject: Elevation coverage in permanently shadowed polar areas
entries.finding: The publisher describes approximately 98 percent coverage with interpolation in permanently shadowed polar areas but supplies no validity mask separating interpolation from stereo samples, so the dataset withholds both caps at latitudes of 60 degrees or more as a conservative display boundary.
entries.revisitWhen: A validity mask separating interpolated from stereo samples is published.

entries.subject: Southern-edge-connected black as a fill indicator
entries.finding: Both pinned rasters have three colour channels and no alpha or validity mask, so southern-edge-connected exact black is used as a conservative indication of fill and marked with the neutral gray grid; the README calls this a heuristic, not a surveyed coverage boundary, and JPEG compression can make fill pixels nonzero.
entries.revisitWhen: A validity mask or alpha channel is published with these maps.

entries.subject: IAU/USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature centre points
entries.finding: Named features use the Ceres centre-point export, snapshot 2026-09-11 and public domain per its FGDC metadata; preparation verifies the archive, reads the attribute table and datum, drops the albedo-feature type code and folds repeated rows, and labels appear at the closest zoom only.

entries.subject: English Wikipedia lead summaries as caption notes
entries.finding: 31 labelled names carry a caption note from the CC BY-SA 4.0 Wikipedia lead summary retrieved 2026-09-12, joined through Wikidata's Gazetteer id property and pinned with the article link and revision.

entries.subject: Vendored JPL body data through the astronomy package
entries.finding: Physical and orbital data come from the vendored JPL body data, Kepler state vectors and IAU rotation, with mean radius 469.7 km and a fixed geometry epoch of 2026-09-03T00:00:00 TT; the mesh is a sphere at that mean radius and claims no resolved shape.

entries.subject: NASA Ceres facts page
entries.finding: The prepared facts summarise the NASA page: asteroid-belt location, Dawn observations, about nine hours per rotation and no moons.

entries.subject: Original crater shadows in the Dawn observations
entries.finding: The lighting decision is to retain the published Dawn observations including their original crater shadows; the optional Shadows setting adds approximate directional illumination and neither mode reconstructs unlit albedo or relights the photographed shadows.

entries.subject: Dawn VIR global band-depth mosaics, 2.7 µm and 3.1 µm (DAWN-A-VIR-5-DDR-CERES-MOSAIC-V1.0)
entries.finding: The archived CMT_MOSAIC-BI_DEPTH and CMT_MOSAIC-BII_DEPTH maps supply the Clay band and Ammonium band datasets, each colored over its own 2nd to 98th percentile (0.229 to 0.283; 0.047 to 0.089) with the rainbow core of Frigeri et al. (2019), Figure 7. On the paper's own ranges most of Ceres sat in the bar's dark ends: the archive (Survey spectra, Ammannito et al. 2016 continuum, no artifact removal) differs from the paper (Survey and HAMO, Carrozzo et al. 2016 correction). A one-cube HAMO reduction with Frigeri's continuum and the public calibration gives a 2.7 um median of 0.272, near the archive's 0.255.

entries.subject: Dawn VIR global band-center mosaics, 2.7 µm and 3.1 µm, in the same data set
entries.finding: The native CMT_MOSAIC-BI_CENTER and CMT_MOSAIC-BII_CENTER maps now supply Clay band centre and Ammonium band centre. Ammannito et al. (2016), LPSC 3020 Figure 2 supplies fixed ranges 2.71–2.75 and 3.02–3.08 micrometres; the display heat palette is authored. Native values and archive artifacts are preserved, with poles and no-data withheld. Nearly uniform absorption wavelength does not measure abundance; the clay-centre median offset from the paper remains unexplained.

entries.subject: Frigeri et al. (2019) 140 m spectral-parameter quadrangle maps as data
entries.finding: The paper says the maps were exported as GeoTIFF, but they are not in the PDS, and the first author's GitHub repository ceres_spectral_parameter_maps holds only a README (last pushed 2017-12-19).
entries.revisitWhen: The maps are released in the PDS or another public archive.

entries.subject: Our own reduction of the Dawn VIR IR cubes with Frigeri et al. (2019) processing, for the Ammonium band
entries.finding: Reduced 1,657 calibrated IR cubes with tools/objects/dawn/vir-mosaic.mts (now packages/bake/authoring/dawn/vir-mosaic.mts): SPICE cameras per line, I/F, stripe and spike removal, phase correction to 30°, footprint mapping, ISIS3 noseam blending. Survey and HAMO set every cell they saw; LAMO, then Approach cubes no coarser than the coarsest Survey cube, fill the gaps; set-aside outlier cubes are levelled by their measured offset and used last. Against Frigeri et al. Figure 7 read back into ranks on 2° cells, the 3.1 µm map scores Spearman 0.89 (archive 0.76) at 98.7% coverage. Averaging LAMO into every cell (0.83) and one flat offset per cube (0.77) scored lower and were dropped. At 2.7 µm ours scores 0.65 against the archive 0.75, so the Clay band keeps the archive. Values stay deeper than the paper because the Carrozzo et al. (2016) response correction was never released.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Hapke model of Li et al. (2019), Table 1, F3 at 749 nm (w 0.139, b 0.364, c 0.048, roughness 19.2 degrees; B0 1.6 and h 0.06 held fixed), fitted to incidence and emission up to 80 degrees and phase from about 7 to about 95 degrees, relative to the flood-lit disc centre. F3 is the colour filter nearest the clear-filter mosaic. Its radiance factor at the flood-lit centre, 0.089, matches the paper's geometric albedo.

entries.subject: Clear-filter Hapke model of Schroeder et al. (2017) as the limb law
entries.finding: Fitted to the same filter as the Monochrome mosaic (w 0.113, B_S0 4.0, h_S 0.02, roughness 22 degrees; incidence and emission below 80 degrees, phase 7.5 to 121 degrees), but its opposition amplitude, which the authors call not physical, gives 0.161 at the flood-lit centre, about twice Ceres's geometric albedo, so every directional frame would be about half as bright relative to the default view.
entries.revisitWhen: A clear-filter fit whose opposition surge is constrained by low-phase data, or a statement that the FC mosaic was corrected with this model.

entries.subject: Shared sphere bank lighting (Lambert with a 0.35 flood floor and 0.05 ambient term, adapted from OpenSpace)
entries.finding: Replaced by the published Hapke law of Li et al. (2019); Ceres now bakes its own bank.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: Dawn radio-science gravity maps of Ceres: radial gravity, its error, Bouguer anomaly and geoid
entries.finding: The PDS4 bundle urn:nasa:pds:dawn-rss-der-ceres 1.0 (doi:10.17189/c2eg-7x61, migrated from PDS3 DAWN-A-RSS-5-CEGR-V4.0, volume DWNCGRS_2 version 4) archives gridded maps only for the degree-18 model CERES18D: JGDWN_CER18D_ACCEL_0018 (radial gravity, degrees 2 to 18 without the hydrostatic J2 and J4, on a 482.0 x 445.9 km ellipsoid), ACCERR_0018 (its one-sigma error from the covariance), BOU_0018 (Bouguer, same degrees), GEOID_0018 and GEOIDERR_0018 (metres above an ellipsoid of a = 482.0 km, f = 0.074896). Each is 181 x 360 little-endian float64, cell centres at whole degrees from 0 E and from 90 N to 90 S; the image bytes are identical in both archives (the MD5 in the PDS4 labels and the PDS3 checksum file agree). The PDS4 labels' value-added corners put the first column's edge at 0 E, half a cell from the producer's PDS3 labels; the PDS3 placement is used and the 360 cells of each pole row are equal, which fixes the rows. Values: radial gravity -272.2 to 212.5 mGal, error 17.6 to 79.0, Bouguer -319.1 to 405.9, geoid -1066.6 to 1454.1 m. Checks against papers: the gravity low and Bouguer high fall on Urvara; Kerwan reads +348 mGal Bouguer (100th percentile), as Bland et al. (2018) infer; Yalode +180; Hanami Planum -225 (4th percentile), the compensated-topography pattern of Park et al. (2016, 2017); Ahuna Mons +153 mGal free-air (99th percentile), where Ruesch et al. (2019) find about 100 mGal at degrees 5 to 14. Ruesch et al. quote about 10 mGal accuracy at the equator for CERES18C; the archived error map gives 17.6 mGal there. Resolution: about 82 km at the equator (degree 18), accurate globally to degree 14, about 105 km. No degree-strength map is archived. Shown as the gravity, gravity-uncertainty, bouguer and geoid datasets through the pds3-grid reader, which needs to accept the detached pointer ("FILE",1).

entries.subject: CERES70E degree-70 gravity model (Park et al. 2020)
entries.finding: The same bundle archives CERES70E, its ISOSIG and KAULA variants as spherical-harmonic coefficients only (data-shadr), with no gridded map. Showing it would need our own summation of the coefficients, which this package does not do.
entries.revisitWhen: A gridded CERES70E product is archived, or a shared coefficient-synthesis capability is approved.

entries.subject: CERES18D geoid error map (JGDWN_CER18D_GEOIDERR_0018)
entries.finding: Archived and decoded (22.0 to 27.4 m, one sigma, nearly uniform) but not shown: it is under 3% of the geoid range and the radial gravity error dataset already shows where the model is weak, as Venus shows only its gravity error.
entries.revisitWhen: Readers ask how far the geoid itself may be off.

entries.subject: Dawn GRaND Ceres derived maps: hydrogen, iron and thermal plus epithermal neutron counts (DAWN GRaND Ceres Bundle 1.0, doi:10.26033/hf9h-pt31)
entries.finding: GRD_HYDROGEN_MAP (wt.% water-equivalent hydrogen, 16.46 to 28.58, sigma about 0.82, a lower bound per the archive), GRD_IRON_MAP (wt.% iron, 13.17 to 17.42, statistical sigma about 0.40) and GRD_TPE_NEUTRON_COUNTS_MAP (counts/s, 2.670 to 3.696, sigma of the mean about 0.02, 276 to 2,885 samples per pixel) are shown as the hydrogen, iron and neutron-counts datasets, grouped with Vesta's as Surface elements. Each table has 110 twenty-degree quasi-equal-area pixels in 10 latitude bands (1, 8, 12, 16, 18, 18, 16, 12, 8, 1 pixels) that tile the sphere exactly; the archive gives a spatial resolution of about 600 km FWHM from LAMO at about 385 km, 2015-12-16 to 2016-05-11. The shared pds-equal-area-table reader samples the containing pixel with no interpolation; the PDS3 labels (DWNCGRD_2) describe their columns inline, which the reader needed to accept. Table bytes match the MD5 in the PDS4 labels. Hydrogen rises from 16.5 at the equator to 28.6 at the north pole while neutron counts fall toward both poles; iron peaks within 20 degrees of the equator. Scales span every value; viridis as on Vesta.

entries.subject: GRD_SMOOTHED_HYDROGEN_MAP, the same hydrogen on 2-degree pixels
entries.finding: The data set catalog says it is the 20-degree counting map smoothed with tesseral spherical harmonics, rebinned to 2 degrees and converted to hydrogen; it carries no new measurement and keeps the 600 km FWHM resolution (16,200 rows, 16.36 to 28.65 wt.% WEH). Showing it beside the 20-degree map would suggest detail the data do not have, so only the measured pixels are shown.
entries.revisitWhen: Readers ask for a smooth hydrogen map, or the archive documents the harmonic degree used.

entries.subject: GRD_IRON_GAMMA_COUNTS_MAP, the 7.6 MeV gamma-ray counting rate
entries.finding: This is the counting rate the iron map was computed from (5.45 to 7.89 counts/min); the iron dataset shows the same information in weight percent. Its PDS3 label names the value columns TPE_COUNTING_RATE and SIG_TPE_COUNTING_RATE, although their descriptions and the PDS4 label call them the Fe 7.6 MeV rate.
entries.revisitWhen: The iron concentration map is superseded or withdrawn.

entries.subject: GRaND data from Dawn's final elliptical orbit (C2E), periapsis under 50 km
entries.finding: The bundle description says these are high spatial-resolution mapping data, but only raw and calibrated counts are archived; the derived collection holds no C2E map. Making one would be our own reduction of GRaND spectra.
entries.revisitWhen: A derived C2E map is archived or published with data.

entries.subject: Dawn FC LAMO clear-filter global mosaic CE_LAMO_G_00N_180E_EQU_CLR.IMG (DAWN-A-FC2-5-CERESMOSAIC-V1.0, volume DWNCLCFC2_2), 35 m/pixel
entries.finding: Its 35 m texels are never drawn. The camera stops at 1.2 Ceres radii from the centre (94 km above the surface) or at maximum zoom 4, whichever is farther; with a focal length of 0.866 times the viewport width, one CSS pixel below the camera covers at least 155 to 169 m (framing reference zoom 1.0 or 1.1, at viewports 710 or 640 CSS px wide), so at two texels per CSS pixel the finest texel shown is 77 to 85 m. At 390 CSS px it is 139 m and at 1440 CSS px 129 to 150 m, the 140 m mosaic's own scale. The product is one 3.56 GB 8-bit image (84,376 x 42,187) whose projection offsets are not whole pixels at 234.37 pixels/degree, which the shared PDS byte reader refuses. See evidence/max-zoom/texels.json.
entries.revisitWhen: The shared camera lets Ceres come closer than 1.2 radii, or the Monochrome atlas is raised past the 140 m mosaic's 21,093 texels around the equator.

entries.subject: Texel size of the shipped Monochrome atlas
entries.finding: The Monochrome dataset is prepared at 4096 texels around the equator (ceres-normal@2x.webp, 4160 x 3072 with gutters, 3,887,406 bytes), 720 m per texel, from a 4096 x 2048 WMS render of the 140 m mosaic. At maximum zoom the camera shows 77 to 173 m per texel depending on the viewport, so the dataset is magnified about 5 to 9 times there. A 16,384-texel atlas (180 m) would be about 62 MB of full-resolution pages and 32,768 (90 m) about 250 MB, if bytes grow with texel count as now, plus about a third more for the reduced levels; first views load only the level the silhouette needs.
entries.revisitWhen: The lead decides on a Monochrome resolutionScale and its source (WMS at a larger size or the native cube).

entries.subject: Ceres Urvara Dawn FC C2E mosaics V1.0 (urn:nasa:pds:dwarf_planet-ceres.dawn-fc.urvara-mosaics)
entries.finding: Controlled clear-filter mosaics of Urvara (128 to 93 W, 59 to 35 S) from 1,583 C2E images at 5 m/pixel, polar stereographic 8-bit GeoTIFF, 2.32 GB for the main mosaic, photometrically corrected with Schroeder et al. (2017, 2018). The repository has a regional route (the Europa normal dataset's detailMosaic inserts controlled GeoTIFFs into the global dataset), but inserted pixels take the global atlas's density, and on Ceres the finest texel the camera ever shows is 77 to 85 m, so 5 m detail cannot appear; resampled that far it holds nothing the LAMO or 140 m mosaics lack. No route lets the camera come closer over one region.
entries.revisitWhen: A shared regional close-zoom route exists (camera below 1.2 radii with regional texture pages).

entries.subject: Occator crater (Cerealia and Vinalia Faculae) XM2 clear-filter mosaic, about 3 m/pixel
entries.finding: The DLR XM2 mosaic used for the Occator geologic maps is not in the Small Bodies Node Dawn FC volumes (checked DWNC*FC2 listings: only global HAMO and LAMO mosaic volumes) or PDS4 Dawn bundles; PIA21924 is a press image without a map frame. Even if released, its detail is below the 77 to 85 m the camera can show.
entries.revisitWhen: A controlled Occator mosaic is archived and a regional close-zoom route exists.

entries.subject: NASA PIA21914 Map of Ceres' Bright Spots (Dawn framing camera)
entries.finding: Global simple-cylindrical picture (2000 x 989 px) with no printed grid. Three gazetteer landmarks (Occator floor, Haulani, Ahuna Mons markers) fit 5.47 px per degree with the left edge near 177.5 E, residuals up to 3.7 px. The markers are not crater centres, so this is only a rough frame check. The content is coloured dots in four classes (floor faculae, rim/wall faculae, bright ejecta, Ahuna Mons) over a camera mosaic. That is a categorical point overlay, not a mapped quantity with a scale and units. As a dataset it would burn dots into a photograph; as features it would need each spot's coordinates, which the figure gives only as digitised dot positions.
entries.revisitWhen: The faculae catalogue behind the figure (coordinates and class for each of the 300+ spots) is found in a published table or archive product, for use as feature content rather than a dataset.

entries.subject: ALMA Ceres Imaging and Spectrum V1.0 (urn:nasa:pds:gbo.ast-ceres.alma.images-spectra::1.0): 265 GHz thermal images as a surface dataset
entries.finding: All 86 calibrated 12-m images (3 epochs: 40 in Oct-Nov 2015, 31 in Sep 2017, 15 in Oct 2017) and the three imaging_parameters tables were read. From the tabulated beam axes and geocentric range, the beam at Ceres is 77-111 km x 63-86 km in 2015, 51-98 x 40-60 km in Sep 2017 and 47-78 x 31-41 km in Oct 2017 (geometric mean 38-96 km). Against the 939.4 km diameter this is 10-25 beams across the disc, about 67-430 beams per disc by area, matching the 10-20 beams the data description states. The app's Dawn 140 m map is 270-690 times finer. Each epoch covers a full rotation (largest sub-Earth longitude gap 55, 62 and 123 degrees; 31 degrees for all epochs combined), but sub-Earth latitude stays between +6.4 and -1.0 degrees, so the poles are only seen at the limb. The disc is dominated by a smooth limb-darkening and diurnal pattern that changes with local time, not location: it spans a median 51%, 31% and 23% of mean disc brightness per epoch. After removing a degree-4 smooth fit inside 0.85 R, the leftover structure is 2.9%, 1.2% and 1.6% RMS (median). The off-disc RMS is 5.4%, 1.1% and 1.5%, and the data description gives 3%, 1% and 2% as imaging artifacts. Surface-fixed test: residual maps rotated to Ceres north and compared between independent epochs looking at the same longitude (within 8 degrees) correlate at median r = 0.04 (n = 101; 0.05 for Sep vs Oct 2017 alone, n = 17). Pairs looking at opposite sides give r = 0.06 (n = 1178). Within one epoch r = 0.61, so the leftover pattern belongs to each epoch's imaging, not to the ground. A surface-fixed thermal map would show about 40-100 km blobs at the artifact level, with no feature that repeats between epochs. Li et al. (2020), the bundle's own paper, reports disc-integrated properties only. The lightcurves and spectrum are disc-integrated and have no surface to map onto. Nothing readable is added to Ceres' surface.
entries.revisitWhen: A published resolved thermal-inertia or emissivity map of Ceres from these ALMA data, or a new ALMA epoch whose surface-fixed residuals repeat between independent epochs.
